chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Say: 'O Allah, expand for me in my sustenance, and extend for me in my lifespan, and forgive me my sin, and make me from those whom You help Your religion with, and do not replace me with another.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for expanding sustenance and extending lifespan in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This supplication, recorded in al-Kafi, encapsulates the Shia tradition of seeking holistic well-being by integrating material needs (sustenance and longevity) with spiritual and political agency (forgiveness and divine victory). It reflects the concept of 'tawassul' through personal piety, where the believer asks to be an instrument of Allah's will, emphasizing that true success lies in serving the religion rather than merely accumulating worldly benefits. The closing plea, 'do not replace me with another,' underscores the value of steadfastness and the fear of losing one's capacity for worship and service.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Expand upon me regarding my sustenance, and Extend to me regarding my life-span, and Forgive my sins for me, and Make me to be from the one whom You<sup>azwj</sup> would be Helping Your<sup>azwj</sup> Religion with’’.
en.sarwar: 27. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Say, ‘O Lord, increase my sustenance, prolong my life, forgive my sins and make me of those whom You employ to support Your religion and do not replace me by others.’”
